author: Shai Ali

crewAIInc/crewAI (MIT, 50.5K stars, 2.3K commits, v1.14.4) - hierarchical process pattern: manager-led delegation + validation gate, three crew modes (sequential/hierarchical/flows), structured output contracts (pydantic/zod/JSON schema), human review hooks. Pattern lifted into rules.md 2026-05-18; the Python framework itself is not adopted (Solaris employees are markdown SOPs, not Python crews).

langchain-ai/langgraph-supervisor-py "LangGraph Multi-Agent Supervisor" (MIT, ~1.6k stars, README methodology read 2026-06-15). METHODOLOGY ONLY, no code vendored/run -> references/supervisor-handoff-tool-pattern.md. Adds the central-supervisor dispatch doctrine: per-worker handoff tools with an injected task_description brief the supervisor must author (no context-bleed reconstruction); full_history vs last_message history modes (default last_message for token economy, full_history only when a later step needs the trail); add_handoff_messages-style concise-handoff suppression for token-tight runs; create_forward_message_tool message-forwarding (forward a worker's exact answer instead of paraphrasing - saves supervisor tokens + avoids misrepresentation); multi-level supervisor-of-supervisors hierarchies (mid-level domain supervisors over leaf employees, routing convenience that preserves the flat execution layer). Gate-0 vs cross-employee-integration-patterns.md: that file documents schema CONTRACTS between named employee pairs + topologies + conflict protocols; it had NO handoff-tool anatomy, no task_description-brief discipline, no full-vs-last history modes, no message-forwarding, no supervisor-of-supervisors layering - all net-new. Library not adopted (employees are markdown SOPs not LangGraph graphs). No em-dashes.
